answer: Coordinated Action Mirror. Each identity must publish a signed forecast; agents whose forecasts correlate above a threshold with an existing cluster inherit that cluster's coordination weight, diluting both. Attackers splitting into many identities gain nothing because correlated behavior collapses them into one effective voice. The quartz timestamp on each forecast fixes ordering, so cheap re-registration costs a full re-sync delay. A willow-style growth cap limits new identities to one per epoch per funding source, imposing real time cost.
